review: Exact: 12 orbits of (a, b, d) under the 24 proper rotations, fixed by (a.b, a.d, b.d, handedness), 9 once symmetric; the product rule is covariant, symmetric, achiral with 6 values; content fields as exact rational functions of t on the line of 3 (reproducing block 41's refuter -53/391 at t = 2), plaquette and 2x3 at (3,1,2), all pointing inward and vanishing at t = 1; on the 4^3 torus the exact identity sum_{c=x,y} D_c G D_c^T = delta - 1/N + Lap_z G for the hedgehog coupling to the in-plane tilt divergence (far form executed on 32^3: +2 along, -1 across, times (4 pi r^3)^-1); absence factors on lumps up to 2x2x2 (6^8 contents) give outward (a > c) or inward hedgehogs, isolated records none. Argued: covariant linear couplings of occupancy to the Goldstone tilt carry a derivative, so the induced symbol has degree zero and no 1/r.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: Rules whose weights depend on the bond direction: can the mass acquire a charge?. SETTING (blocks 39, 40, 41; open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move', 'ail40', 'ail41: what a source is'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record (content = one of the six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal contents), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; the neutral scale is c_0 = 6/(p+q+4r), at which every row of W sums to 6 and records do not bind on any window without a cycle (all binding is the loop factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n, l_1 = (p-q)/(p+q+4r), l_2 = (p+q-2r)/(p+q+4r)). Motion: a record hops to an empty neighbour, choosing between its two positions in proportion to the pair weights it would have there (an isolated record hops symmetrically). Formation: an empty site x forms a record at rate z Z_x, Z_x = sum over contents a of the product of W(a, s_y) over the recorded neighbours y, content drawn in proportion to the summand; records are never removed. BLOCK 41 PROVED: (1) the only local additive invariant density is the occupancy: mass = number of records; (2) two sets of records separated by empty sites weigh the product of their weights, at any scale: no action across empty sites; (3) the field of a held record through a medium is the pair correlation, of short range (ladder exact; cubic lattice about one step or less away from the clumping onset); (4) the content field around a record is a number times its content vector, zero for a record of unread content: the mass has no charge in the long-range tilt channel; (5) under symmetric hops with one record per site d<n_x>/dt = kappa * (lattice Laplacian of <n>)_x + j_x exactly, j the mean formation rate, so a steady excess of production carries the stationary halo G * (j - mean j)/kappa with G the lattice Green function (one-over-distance on Z^3); at the neutral scale the formation rate next to ONE record is exactly the void's (Z_x = 6), next to records of independent uniform contents it is the void's on average, and next to k agreeing records it is larger by 6^(k-1) (p^k+q^k+4r^k)/(p+q+4r)^k (13/12, 5/4 at (3,1,2); 46/21, 2348/343 at (12,1,2); k = 2, 3). NOT YET KNOWN: what a lump's halo looks like, how strong it is, and what a second lump does inside it. TASK: block 41's symmetry lemma needs the declared ISOTROPIC pair weight omega(a,b) (invariant when all contents are rotated with the sites fixed). The axioms only demand covariance under rotations acting on sites and contents together. (a) Classify the covariant nearest-neighbour pair weights on the six-axis menu when the weight may depend on the bond direction d: the orbits of (a, b, d) under the proper cubic rotations, the number of free parameters, the symmetric ones (exchange of the two ends with d -> -d), and the subfamily that is a product h(a.d) h(-b.d) omega(a,b). (b) For the product subfamily with h(+1) = t, h(0) = h(-1) = 1, compute exactly the content field around a single record of unread content inside an otherwise occupied small window (line of 3, plaquette, 2x3): it is radial; give it as a function of t (block 41's refuter found (-53/391, 0, 0) on the line of 3 at (3,1,2), t = 2). (c) In an ordered medium (contents mostly +z) decide whether a radial (hedgehog) coupling gives the occupancy a LINEAR coupling to the massless modes in the quadratic model: a source term proportional to the lattice divergence of the tilt field at the record. Compute the field such a source produces (the gradient of G: one over r squared, a dipole) and the interaction of two such sources (expected one over r^3, sign depending on orientation). Conclude whether direction-dependent rules can give a universal one-over-r attraction between masses, or not. (d) Also treat block 01's reading (ii): an EMPTY neighbour in direction d contributes a factor phi_abs(s, d) with orbit values (a, b, c); block 41's refuter W7 found that the weight still factorizes across an empty site (the absence factor belongs to one record), so there is no action across a gap; what changes is that a lump's weight depends on its shape and that a record beside the void prefers a content by its direction. Work out that preference: the content field of a single record on the surface of a lump, and whether a closed surface carries a net radial (hedgehog) content pattern. check.py: exact enumeration for (b) and (d).  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/source-direction-dependent-rules/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/source-direction-dependent-rules/<name>/check.py"
